city_info.name: New Haven
city_info.motto: Ipsa scientia potestas est (Knowledge itself is power)

landmarks.name: Yale University
landmarks.note: One of the oldest universities in America

landmarks.name: New Haven Green
landmarks.note: One of the oldest public parks in America, site of many historic events

landmarks.name: Shubert Theatre
landmarks.note: Known as 'Birthplace of the Nation's Greatest Hits'

historical_dates.event: New Haven Colony founded by English Puritans led by Theophilus Eaton and John Davenport
Yale University founded (originally Collegiate School) in Saybrook, later moved to New Haven
New Haven incorporated as a city
Amistad trial begins in New Haven, a landmark case for abolition
First public library in Connecticut opens in New Haven
New Haven's first public high school opens
Armistice Day - World War I ends, celebrated on New Haven Green
Yale Bowl hosts first football game
Declaration of Independence signed (New Haven celebrates with annual parade)
First Continental Congress delegates from Connecticut meet in New Haven
New Haven volunteers march to Lexington and Concord
British forces raid New Haven during Revolutionary War
New Haven Railroad opens, connecting city to New York
First electric streetcar runs in New Haven
